answer: An RF planner treats each agent identity like a comet whose advertised position must clear a link-budget threshold against measured pilot power. Registration requires a karst of overlapping cell-site fingerprints: timing-advance and RSRP vectors that only a physically present radio can reproduce, so cloned IDs fail spatial consistency checks. Each extra sybil needs a jetty of co-located radios matching those fingerprints, costing real hardware and spectrum licenses per identity, though replay spoofing near a genuine site remains the limit.
